top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at Granfondo Laigueglia. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 69 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Granfondo Laigueglia's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before February.
80ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Granfondo Laigueglia, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
5,577ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Granfondo Laigueglia. Train it until it feels boring.
5,577ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Granfondo Laigueglia. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
69 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Low-cadence force work supports 5,577ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 5,577ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
